correctness.rationale: A complete epsilon-NFA precisely models interleavings of one erased three-symbol pattern and an output with a finite alternating host. Subset determinization counts distinct outputs. For each of the eight patterns and both host parities, an exact integer certificate verifies q consecutive zero fourth differences of the transfer sequence (q=9 or 10 reachable states); Cayley-Hamilton then forces zero fourth differences for every length. The initial four coefficients determine all sixteen rational series and coefficient formulas. Standalone integer code and direct exhaustive position-deletion enumeration through length 24 both replayed successfully; finite tests alone are not taken as proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The primary 2026 paper provides algorithms for computing each finite C(w,u) and specific singleton structural assertions, not an all-length eight-pattern count. The fixed-composition spectrum aggregates over every deletion of a given size, without retaining the order of the prescribed erased triple; the patterns 001,010,100 have equal composition yet distinct explicit counts here. Its stronger host-length scope therefore does not supply the present ordered-pattern enumeration.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither an all-alternating subsequence (01)^k count (length is always even), nor a length-two arbitrary-host deletion count, implies the odd three-letter case via their hypotheses. The output-composition identity does not distinguish deletion patterns of the same Parikh vector; indeed the new even-source counts of 001 and 100 differ by n-1+binom(n-2,2), whereas their deleted compositions agree. The new table has independent order-sensitive information not supplied by these earlier claims.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary 2026 complement-factor paper and the closest published result statements do not cover the complete ordered length-three deletion table. An earlier alternating-host result only erases (ab)^k (even length), an arbitrary-host result only erases two letters, and a composition-refined result aggregates all deletion patterns of given size and does not distinguish their order. Primary full text and relevant published result documents were inspected, and semantic and exact web searches were conducted; historical priority remains uncertain.

value.rationale: This is the first nontrivial odd-length prescribed deletion layer for the natural finite alternating-word family, and the theorem gives a complete classification across all eight patterns, every host length and both phases. Its exact rational enumerators and universal one-output differences distinguish specified deletion order from coarse composition-only spectra. The all-length parity boundary, not a hand-picked sample, is the motivating invariant; no general algorithmic speedup is claimed.
